standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of quasi-compactness through finite subcovers of open coverings, and the induced topology on a subset
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on quasi-compact spaces and maps, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the procedure by which an open covering of the subset is enlarged to one of the whole space.

core_obligations: Enlarge the covering: for an open covering of the closed subset the proof chooses open subsets of the ambient space whose intersections with the subset are the given members (proof lines 1884-1886).
Cover the whole space: adding the complement of the closed subset gives an open covering of the quasi-compact space (proof lines 1886-1887).

Extract a finite subcover: quasi-compactness supplies finitely many members covering the space, and discarding the complement leaves finitely many of the original members covering the subset (proof lines 1887-1890).
Conclusion: the closed subset is quasi-compact (proof line 1890).
proof_roadmap: 取 E 的开覆盖 E = ⋃V_j，选 X 中开集 U_j 使 V_j = E ∩ U_j。
加入 X \ E 得到 X 的开覆盖，由 X 准紧取有限子覆盖，去掉 X \ E 后剩下的有限多个 V_j 覆盖 E。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the standard inheritance of quasi-compactness by closed subsets (author lemma at source lines 1878-1881, label lemma-closed-in-quasi-compact). The proof (source lines 1883-1891) enlarges an open covering of the subset to one of the ambient space by adding the complement, applies quasi-compactness, and discards the added member (proof lines 1884-1890). Together with the companion statement that quasi-compact subsets of a Hausdorff space are closed, this is the pair used throughout the chapter's compactness arguments. H2.
